title: Assemble a rack-and-pinion parallel gripper, seating the second rack at the tooth that centres its jaws
instruction: Seat the loose orange rack on the pinion so the gripper's two fingers sit evenly about its centre, then pull the white finger at least 15 mm further open, without touching the orange rack, and let go.
context: Synchronised parallel grippers, pneumatic or electric (e.g. Festo HPPF, rack-and-pinion jaw drive), keep both jaws centred with one pinion between two racks; building or re-building such a gripper means seating the second rack at the tooth that matches the other finger's measured opening, read from the scene. Any other tooth still meshes but leaves the jaws 4.7 mm off-centre, biasing every grasp made with that hardware.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the table top. Gripper housing, free on the table, centre (240, 0) on four tape corner marks, long side along y: dark printed PETG floor 160 x 52 mm on a 6 mm steel bar (460 g in all), walls 12 mm tall, inner faces 45 mm apart, a 5 mm rail under each rack, stop blocks at y +40 to +44 (white channel) and -44 to -40 (orange), a 1 mm yellow scale along each wall top. Pinion at the centre, free on an M4 shoulder screw: 27 mm disc, 4 mm thick, holding eight 3 x 16 mm steel dowel pins 3.5 mm deep on a 24 mm circle (9.42 mm pitch), 10 g. Racks: printed PETG, 88 mm, 12 mm tall, 13 g, tooth gaps 3.4 mm (0.4 mm backlash), rounded crests, a 7.5 x 6 x 30 mm finger plate at the outer end, a 7 x 6 x 19.5 mm finger-mount boss on top. White rack: near channel (x 228), one tooth (9.4 mm) open from its stop. Orange rack: loose on the table at x 252, y 140, teeth toward -x.
scoring: From a top photo (wall scales), a straightedge, a hand check and the video. 0 unless both racks are in mesh with the pinion: seated in their channels (top flush with the pins within 1.5 mm, against the wall within 1.5 mm, level within 3 deg, straight within 4 deg), over the pinion (its axis between the rack's first and last tooth) with a pin in a tooth gap; and centred: |s_white - s_orange| / 2 at most 2.0 mm (s = finger travel from its stop; one tooth off is 4.7 mm). 1.0: also each rack travelled 15 mm apart while the orange rack was untouched (video), both fingers 15 mm open, then released, still, grippers 30 mm clear, for 4 s. 0.5: in mesh and centred otherwise. Mesh check after the photo: pushing the white finger 5 mm (toward its stop, or outward if under 5 mm open) moves the orange one 5 mm the same way (within 2 mm) on the scales; if it doesn't, 0.
reset_notes: Lift the orange rack out and stand it on its mark; slide the white rack to its stop, then open it one tooth (9.4 mm on its scale); put the housing back on its tape marks.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX with the printed parts' real sizes and masses (housing 460 g, racks 13 g, pinion 10 g) and the real 0.4 mm backlash. Teeth and chamfers are stepped boxes (true chamfers in gripper.scad); pins are 3 mm cylinders with rounded tops. Seating, meshing and the coupled drive are contacts, not rules; the scorer reads mesh from the rack poses and the pinion angle. Rack friction 0.25. The cover and actuator are omitted: the gripper is assembled bare.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms rose 20-34 cm above the table and hovered, the left arm beside the orange rack, the right beside the white one, never closer than about 23 cm, nothing touched); scripted demo: 1.0 (orange rack in mesh at the centring tooth, |d| 0.12 mm, success at step 559 after 4 s hold)
